plot_spatial_pair <- function(data, k) {
  samples <- c("BALBc-1", "MRL-4")
  domain <- factor(data$domain, levels = seq.int(0L, k - 1L))
  palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(k, "Dynamic")
  symbols <- rep(c(16, 17, 15, 18, 3, 4, 8, 1, 2, 6, 0), length.out = k)
  old <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old))
  graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  titles <- c("BALBc-1", "MRL-4 (early)")
  for (i in seq_along(samples)) {
    keep <- as.character(data$sample) == samples[[i]]
    graphics::plot(
      data$x[keep], data$y[keep], asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
      xlab = "", ylab = "", pch = symbols[as.integer(domain[keep])], cex = 0.17,
      col = palette[as.integer(domain[keep])],
      main = paste0(titles[[i]], " (K=", k, ")")
    )
    graphics::box(col = "grey70")
  }
  invisible(palette)
}

matrix_long <- function(x, value_name, condition = NULL) {
  result <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(x)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(result) <- c("source", "target", value_name)
  if (!is.null(condition)) result$condition <- condition
  result
}

plot_enrichment_dotplot <- function(enrichment, k) {
  values <- as.matrix(enrichment$enrichment)
  size_threshold <- 0.58
  color_threshold <- 0.58

  # CellCharter v0.2.0 defaults to cluster_labels=TRUE. Its complete-linkage
  # clustering uses the thresholded color matrix, not the raw enrichment.
  color_values <- ifelse(
    values < 0, -1,
    ifelse(values < color_threshold, 0, 1)
  )
  domain_order <- colnames(values)
  if (ncol(values) > 1L) {
    domain_order <- domain_order[stats::hclust(
      stats::dist(t(color_values)), method = "complete"
    )$order]
  }

  cells <- expand.grid(
    cell_type = rownames(values), domain = colnames(values),
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  cells$value <- as.vector(values)
  # CellCharter maps [-1, 0.58] through TwoSlopeNorm. Scanpy 1.9.3 then
  # clips negative dot-size fractions to zero and uses area = fraction^1.5.
  # Base R `cex` scales diameter, hence exponent 1.5 / 2 = 0.75 here.
  cells$size <- pmax(0, pmin(cells$value, size_threshold)) / size_threshold
  cells$color_value <- as.vector(color_values)
  palette <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
    c("#3B4CC0", "darkgrey", "#B40426")
  )(101)
  color_index <- pmax(
    1L, pmin(101L, round((cells$color_value + 1) * 50) + 1L)
  )
  graphics::plot(
    as.integer(factor(cells$cell_type, levels = rownames(values))),
    as.integer(factor(cells$domain, levels = domain_order)),
    pch = 21, bg = palette[color_index], col = "black",
    cex = 2.5 * cells$size^0.75, axes = FALSE,
    xlim = c(0.5, nrow(values) + 9),
    xlab = "", ylab = "Spatial domain (complete-linkage order)",
    main = paste0("Cluster ~ full cell type enrichment (K=", k, ")")
  )
  graphics::axis(
    1, at = seq_len(nrow(values)), labels = rownames(values),
    las = 2, cex.axis = 1
  )
  graphics::axis(
    2, at = seq_along(domain_order), labels = domain_order, las = 1
  )
  graphics::box()
  graphics::mtext("Cell type", side = 1, line = 16)
  graphics::legend(
    x = nrow(values) + 1, y = max(seq_along(domain_order)), xjust = 0,
    legend = c("depleted", "positive < 0.58", "enriched >= 0.58"),
    pt.bg = c("#3B4CC0", "darkgrey", "#B40426"),
    pch = 21, cex = 1, title = "log2 observed/expected", bty = "n"
  )
}

plot_heatmap <- function(x, title, limits = NULL, annotate = FALSE,
                         pvalue = NULL, significance = NULL) {
  x <- as.matrix(x)
  plotted <- x
  plotted[!is.finite(plotted)] <- NA_real_
  if (is.null(limits)) {
    limits <- range(plotted, finite = TRUE)
  }
  if (length(limits) != 2L || any(!is.finite(limits)) || limits[[1L]] >= 0 ||
      limits[[2L]] <= 0) {
    stop("Heatmap limits must be finite and span zero, as required by TwoSlopeNorm.")
  }
  palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(101, "Blue-Red 3", rev = TRUE)
  graphics::image(
    seq_len(ncol(plotted)), seq_len(nrow(plotted)), t(plotted),
    col = palette, zlim = limits, axes = FALSE,
    xlab = "target domain", ylab = "source domain", main = title,
    useRaster = TRUE
  )
  graphics::axis(
    1, at = seq_len(ncol(plotted)), labels = colnames(plotted), las = 2
  )
  graphics::axis(
    2, at = seq_len(nrow(plotted)), labels = rownames(plotted), las = 2
  )
  graphics::box()
  if (annotate) {
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(plotted))) for (j in seq_len(ncol(plotted))) {
      if (!is.finite(plotted[i, j])) next
      significant <- !is.null(pvalue) && !is.null(significance) &&
        is.finite(pvalue[i, j]) && pvalue[i, j] <= significance
      label <- paste0(sprintf("%.2f", plotted[i, j]), if (significant) "*" else "")
      graphics::text(j, i, label, cex = 1)
    }
  }
}

1 Scope and artifact roles

This report consumes regenerated outputs under a new result root. The frozen Phase-0 report and artifacts are provisional/stale and are not used here. The primary result is whatever K the R AutoK run selected independently; it is never fixed to K=4 or K=11. The K=11 panel is a separate torch_gmm_fit() sensitivity fit corresponding to Cluster(n_clusters=11, random_state=12345). Its integer seed is matched, but R and Python use different initialization and random-number streams, so this does not claim seed-identical fitted parameters. Published H5AD cluster_cellcharter labels are retained only as a third reference artifact and are not plotted as the R tutorial fit.

role_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(manifest$roles, function(x) data.frame(
  role_id = x$role_id,
  k = x$k,
  seed = if (is.na(x$seed)) "NA (not an R fit)" else as.character(x$seed),
  model_path = if (is.na(x$model_path)) "NA (published labels)" else x$model_path,
  cell_order_sha256 = x$cell_order_sha256,
  aggregation_data_id = x$aggregation_data_id,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)))

Only BALBc-1 and early MRL-4 are displayed in maps. Enrichment and proximity statistics use all nine libraries. The full cell_type annotation is used for the log2 observed/expected dot plot with size_threshold=0.58, color_threshold=0.58, and the CellCharter v0.2.0 default clustered labels.

2 AutoK stability and K selection

The points are all saved neighboring-K Fowlkes–Mallows comparisons from the seven repeated fits; the line is their mean. K=1 is shown as non-estimable because this criterion requires fitted solutions on both neighboring K values. K=4 is the independently selected global maximum. K=11 is annotated only as the predeclared tutorial-matched sensitivity and lies on the secondary K=10–11 stability shoulder.

knitr::include_graphics(manifest$autok_stability_plot)

3.4 Differential neighborhood enrichment in both display directions

Both panels reuse one sample-level permutation result (n_perms=100). A star marks directional empirical p <= 0.05; reversing the display negates only the effect and reuses the same permutation counts and p-values.

graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1))
plot_heatmap(
  primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL vs BALBc", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)
plot_heatmap(
  primary_balbc_mrl$effect, "BALBc vs MRL", annotate = TRUE,
  pvalue = primary_balbc_mrl$pvalue, significance = 0.05
)

primary_diff_table <- matrix_long(primary_mrl_balbc$effect, "MRL_minus_BALBc")
primary_diff_table$empirical_pvalue <- as.vector(primary_mrl_balbc$pvalue)
knitr::kable(primary_diff_table,
             caption = "Values underlying the primary differential heatmaps")

)

)

)

5 Interpretation boundary

The R-selected AutoK K remains the only primary result. K=11 is a separately fitted tutorial sensitivity analysis. The published H5AD labels remain a separate reference artifact. Representation-learning equivalence is not claimed because the supplied trVAE representation is treated as immutable input. Spatial panels use base-R rendering of the exact coordinates and labels rather than Squidpy’s plotting stack, so pixel-level visual equivalence is not claimed.
